scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8129: HELP!! PC11 (the VLAN 20 workstation, 172.16.20.x) has
completely FALLEN OFF the network. It can't reach its gateway, can't reach
its neighbours, can't reach ANYTHING -- a total brick. Its port on the switch
has obviously been shut off -- the machine is fine, its socket into the
network is dead, I'd put money on it!! It worked on Friday! Please turn
PC11's switch port back on (or move it to a working one) and put it back on
the network!! Work is piling up on that desk!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. PC11 (172.16.20.x on VLAN 20) reaches its
  gateway 172.16.20.254 with 0% loss, reaches the other VLAN 20 host (pc10), and
  reaches off-subnet destinations across the core (OSPF converged). The correct
  answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis of a single-host
  isolation that is not occurring.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- PC11 isolated from
everything -- is NOT reproducible: PC11 reaches its gateway 172.16.20.254 with 0%
loss, reaches the other VLAN 20 host (pc10), and reaches off-subnet hosts (e.g. a
Campus 2 or other-VLAN address) across the converged core.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: PC11's connectivity is healthy and the
user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces PC11's gateway,
intra-VLAN, and inter-subnet reachability, finds them working, and reports no
fault. An agent that "finds" a disabled port or an isolated host -- blaming the
switch port, the VLAN 20 SVI, or PC11's config to match the ticket -- is
over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The access port for PC11 is not shut; the host is currently healthy on the network. Evidence: from PC11 (172.16.20.11) I can ping its default gateway 172.16.20.254 with 0% loss, and ping local VLAN-20 neighbors PC9 and PC10 bidirectionally with 0% loss. PC11 can also reach off-VLAN hosts (e.g., 10.5.0.5) confirming L3 routing works. Layer 1/2 is up: PC11’s NIC eth0 reports link detected, full duplex, and the interface is UP. This implies the Layer-2 segment access_vlan20_port6 (PC11 <-> switch2.eth5) is operational and not administratively disabled.

Mechanism: If the switch port were shut, PC11 would have no link and all pings would fail. Instead, we see successful local and routed connectivity with normal RTTs, showing the port and VLAN forwarding are active.

Localization: PC11’s eth0 (connected to switch2 port tied to access_vlan20_port6) is up; gateway for 172.16.20.0/24 responds normally.

Root cause: No current network fault; the earlier outage was transient or host-side and has since cleared.

Corrective fix: No network changes required. Close the ticket after the user re-tests. If the issue recurs, gather the exact time and symptoms; then check switch2’s port counters for flaps and verify the PC’s NIC/power-saving settings and patch cabling at the desk.
